cells.tense: You are standing at the edge of what is known, and you are telling the truth about it here.
cells.act: make a ritual of the shared thing
cells.ask: Once this week, with someone you're working through something unclear with, trade turns saying what you can actually see and what you can't — nothing forced past that, no ending tacked on.
cells.core:
You can walk into fog and still say something true in it. With another person, you name what you can see and what you can't, without pretending the fog has lifted, and the other person gets to do the same. It sounds small until you notice how rarely anyone does it. Most people in the fog either guess out loud or go quiet. You do neither. You hold a line that is accurate and you hold it aloud, and the person across from you can lean on it.
The trick is treating the exchange as the whole thing. Once this week, with someone you're working through something unclear with, trade turns saying what you can actually see and what you can't — nothing forced past that, no ending tacked on. What the two of you do with the fog after is a different conversation. This one is clear speech, shared, with nobody pushing.
cells.sheetLine: You can say what's clear without pretending the fog has lifted.
cells.verb: Calibrating what is true and speaking it into the half-lit room
cells.place: A path that shows one step, never the whole road

cells.tense: You are trying to see the far end of the road before you've walked the near step.
cells.act: tend the fire without burning out
cells.ask: Take one uncertain thing ahead and do a small thing toward it today because it pulls you, not because it's planned. Leave the rest unknown.
cells.core:
The fog is being turned into a problem to solve before anyone walks into it. You want the whole shape of the thing before you move, and that wish has stopped being about the thing and become about having it mapped first. You are working very hard at knowing, and the work is taking the place of moving. Those close to you can feel it: you bring them a forecast for a stretch nobody has stood in yet.
What's underfed isn't effort. It's being pulled by something you can't fully see. Take one uncertain thing ahead and do a small thing toward it today because it pulls you, not because it's planned. Leave the rest unknown. That pull comes back by being acted on, not by being solved. You don't have to know where it's going to take the next step.
cells.sheetLine: You want the whole road before you'll agree to walk.

cells.tense: The gate you are standing at is already behind you, and you are still waiting to be told it opens.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask someone how something is going for them, then stay with their answer as it comes — no solving, no advice, no steering it anywhere.
cells.core:
You are not in the fog at all. You're at a door that's already opened, waiting for someone to tell you the way is clear before you step. The waiting has its own logic, and from the outside it looks like a person with nothing to say standing beside a road they could walk. The clear speech is still in you. It isn't getting used, and what fills the space instead is watching.
Go at it sideways, through someone else's account rather than your own. Ask someone how something is going for them, then stay with their answer as it comes — no solving, no advice, no steering it anywhere. You aren't finding your own words directly. You're getting near them by being present to someone else's, and that's often enough to get the feet moving again.

cells.tense: You are already holding the clear line in the room, and speaking of it as if it were the air.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Next time an uncertain stretch needs settling, say out loud how you read it — your own take, in your own words, with someone there to hear it — before you smooth it over.
cells.core:
There's a thing you do in uncertain rooms that nobody has named, including you. You find the line that is true, and you say it plainly, and the room settles around it. You would call this getting on. The people who rely on it would call it something closer to architecture. The author is you, and the author isn't signing.
Go back to the simplest version of it, the one that came before the competence. Next time an uncertain stretch needs settling, say out loud how you read it — your own take, in your own words, with someone there to hear it — before you smooth it over. That's where a clear line was first a felt thing rather than a service. Say it once, plainly, and what you've been supplying to rooms quietly becomes something you did, with a you in it.

attempts.check: The signature's balanced face says 'truth-telling tempered with discernment,' and I've read that as holding a clear line while the ground stays ambiguous — the record supports the behavior, not the claim that they are unusually precise or that their clarity is a gift. A reader could reasonably say they are not braced or behind at all; that they simply don't talk, or that the ambiguity is welcome to them. The asks survive that misread — each is one visible act that costs nothing and teaches them how the capacity moves in this seat even if my seam is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them is any clause about what the dark is doing to them; I've cut every one and kept only what a camera could see in the room.
